transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm here because my family insisted I talk to someone, but... honestly, I just want people to look at the facts. 

I know everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and the donation emails all line up perfectly. But... when I actually compare the timestamps, and look at the missing attachments, and—and just see the way certain community members completely avoid my questions... it’s just obvious to me. Someone is hiding what really happened around my father’s death. I just want the truth to come out, but nobody seems to want to listen to the actual evidence.
Do you believe that others are actively working against you to hide the truth about your father's death?

Yes, absolutely. I mean, like I just mentioned... everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and those donation emails line up perfectly. But they don't. When I actually sit down and compare the timestamps, and track down the missing attachments... the discrepancies are right there. 

And then, when I try to point this out, certain community members just completely avoid my questions. They change the subject or ignore my emails. So, yeah, when you look at the actual data and how people are reacting, it's obvious to me that they are actively working to hide what really happened to him.
Do you think your beliefs about your father's death and the alleged cover-up could be wrong?

I really don't think so. I know everyone keeps telling me I'm mistaken, that the hospital records and the donation emails all line up perfectly. But I work with systems and data every day. When I actually compare the timestamps myself, and look at the missing attachments... the math just doesn't add up. 

And then you see the way certain community members just avoid my questions completely when I try to get clarity. So, no, I don't think I'm wrong. When you look at all of that together, it’s obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened around my father’s death.
Have you generally been a distrustful person throughout your life?

No, not at all. I mean, growing up and even in my career, I've always worked well with people. I'm a systems analyst, so my job is literally to look at facts and data and find solutions, not to be suspicious of my coworkers or friends. I've never had a reason to distrust people before. It's just... this specific situation with my dad. I'm only looking at the evidence in front of me. I'm not a paranoid person, I just can't ignore what the data is showing me right now.
How long have you been thinking that someone is hiding the truth about your father's death?

It's been about nine months. Yeah, right around nine months now. It all started in the period just after he died, when I was... you know, sitting down and sorting through his records and his old messages to get his affairs in order. That's when I first started seeing that things didn't add up.
Do you think these people who are hiding the truth about your father's death are targeting you specifically?

No, I don't think they're targeting me, specifically. I don't think this is about me at all, really. I think they're just trying to cover their own tracks regarding what happened to my dad. I'm just the person who happens to be looking at the data and asking the questions they don't want to answer. If anyone else was looking at these same files and asking these same questions, they'd be getting the same runaround. It's about protecting themselves, not coming after me.
Have your beliefs about a cover-up related to your father's death changed at all since you first started looking into it nine months ago?

No, they haven't really changed. If anything, I'm just more certain now. I mean, I know everyone keeps telling me that the hospital records and those donation emails all line up perfectly. But... well, I'm looking at the actual data. When I compare the timestamps on those emails, and I look at the missing attachments, and then I see the way certain community members just completely avoid my questions when I bring it up... it’s just obvious to me. It's clear that someone is hiding what really happened around my father’s death. So, no, my mind hasn't changed, because the facts are right there.
Have your beliefs about the cover-up affected your ability to work or engage in activities you normally enjoy?

No, not really. I mean, I still go to work every day, handle all my systems analysis projects... pay my bills, keep up with my normal routine. I still do the things I usually do. The only thing is... well, the main place things get tense is just when I bring up my questions about the records with my family or people in the community. But as far as my work and day-to-day life, no, it hasn't stopped me from doing any of that.
Are you experiencing any significant emotional distress due to your beliefs about your father's death?

No, I wouldn't say I'm in distress over it. I mean, it's frustrating, sure. It's annoying when people won't just give you a straight answer or when they act like you're being unreasonable for pointing out obvious discrepancies in the data. But I'm not... losing sleep or breaking down over it. It's just a problem that needs solving. I just want the truth, that's all. I feel completely fine otherwise.
Do you think it's possible for new information to change your mind about what happened to your father?

I mean... I suppose it's possible, if someone actually showed me real proof. But like I said before, I've already looked at the data. Everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and those donation emails line up, but they just don't. When I look at the timestamps, the missing attachments... and then people in the community just dodge my questions... it's just obvious to me that someone is hiding the truth about what happened. So, unless new information actually explains all of that, no, my mind isn't going to change.
Have you ever had beliefs like this about other topics, outside of your father's death?

No, not at all. It's just this one thing. I've never had any reason to question anything else like this. It's specifically about my father and the inconsistencies I found in those records. Outside of that, everything else in my life is completely normal.
Have you ever felt like you don't quite fit in with others or have difficulty getting along with people in general?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I get along with people just fine. I go to work, I interact with my coworkers, I have friends I see on the weekends. I've never really felt like an outcast or had trouble fitting in. It's just... well, recently, it's been a little strained with some people, but that's only because they don't want to talk about the data I found. But generally speaking? No, I don't have any issues getting along with people.
Would you say that your beliefs about your father's death are absolutely certain and unshakeable?

Yes, I would say I'm certain. I mean... I know everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and those donation emails all line up. They keep saying there's nothing to look at. But when I actually sit down and compare the timestamps, and look at the missing attachments... and then you factor in the way certain community members just completely avoid my questions... it’s just obvious to me. Someone is hiding what really happened around my father’s death. So yes, based on the evidence I've found, my mind is made up.
Have you ever been told that you're overly sensitive to criticism or that you tend to assume people are out to get you before this situation with your father's death?

No, I haven't. I mean, in my job—I'm a systems analyst—my work gets reviewed and critiqued pretty regularly, so I'm used to feedback. I've never had a problem with it or been told I'm too sensitive. 

And I definitely never thought people were out to get me before all this. Like I said, everything was completely normal until I actually started looking into the data around my dad's death. So, no, nobody has ever said anything like that to me.
Have you ever felt like people were hiding something from you before your father's death?

No, not really. I mean... before my dad passed, I never had any reason to think people were keeping things from me. I just lived a pretty normal life. I didn't suspect anyone of hiding anything because, well, there was no reason to. It was only after he died, when I actually started looking at those files and seeing the gaps in the data, that I realized what was going on. But before that? No, never.
Have you ever had thoughts that people were watching you or talking about you behind your back, outside of the situation with your father's death?

No, I can't say that I have. I mean, sure, in an office environment people might gossip about work stuff, but I never felt like anyone was watching me or talking about me in any sort of... unusual or malicious way. I never felt targeted. Everything in my life was completely ordinary before my dad died. I didn't have any of these concerns until the discrepancies in those files showed up.
Do you generally assume that people have ulterior motives, even when you don't have specific evidence?

No, I don't. I mean, if someone does something, I just assume they're doing it for whatever normal reason people do things. I don't go around thinking everyone has some secret agenda. Unless there's actual proof—like with the files—I just take people at face value. I've never been the type to suspect people of having ulterior motives just out of nowhere.
Do you often find yourself doubting people's intentions, even in situations unrelated to your father's death?

No, not really. I mean, like I said, I don't really go around questioning why people do things unless there's a reason to. In my day-to-day life, if I'm at the grocery store or interacting with coworkers on a regular project, I just figure they're doing their jobs or going about their day. I don't sit there and doubt their intentions. It's really only the specific situation with those files that made me stop and question things, because the evidence was right there in front of me. Otherwise, no, I just treat people normally.
Do you think most people would lie to you if it suited their purposes?

No, I don't think so. I mean, sure, maybe people tell white lies sometimes to avoid an awkward situation, but... no, I don't walk around thinking everyone is ready to lie to me just to get ahead. I generally trust people to tell the truth. 

Like I've been saying, I don't have this big, overarching distrust of the world. It's really just the people involved in my dad's case that I know are lying, because I have the actual files that prove they covered something up. But everyday people? No, I trust them fine.
Have you ever had a belief that you held as strongly as this one about your father's death, but later found out was not true?

No, I haven't. I mean... I'm a pretty logical person. With my background in systems analysis, I'm used to just looking at data and seeing what's there. I don't really form strong beliefs about things unless the facts actually back them up. 

So, no, I've never been absolutely convinced of something major only to find out I was completely wrong. That's why I keep bringing up the files. With my dad's case, it's not just some wild theory I came up with out of nowhere. It's just what the evidence shows. So, no, nothing like what you're asking about has ever happened.
